_doc: Revert-verify mutants for issue #4359 — a template slot that renders to nothing must not yield a "computed" definition. M1 restores the pre-fix state verbatim. M2 is the WRONG fix the AC forbids (guard keyed on the literal `differentia` key instead of on the template's slots): it satisfies D1/D2 and fails ONLY on a spec naming another property, which is exactly what D3 exists to catch. Run: python3 -I ~/.claude/bin/mutant-driver.py <this file> after setting `tree`/`subject` to YOUR checkout.
subject: <ABSOLUTE PATH TO YOUR exocortex CHECKOUT>/packages/obsidian-plugin/src/domain/concept-definition/ConceptDefinitionResolver.ts

M1_no_slot_guard._note: The pre-fix state: the render is returned whenever it trims non-empty, so `"{{differentia}} {{genus}}"` with no differentia yields the parent's bare label and shadows the stored narrative.
M1_no_slot_guard._note_anchor: Anchor re-pointed after review LOW-2 replaced the nullable-object `stats` with three primitives; the guard's SEMANTICS are unchanged, only its expression (§A71 — my own edit invalidated the anchor, not drift in someone else's code).

M2_guard_keyed_on_differentia_name._note: The wrong fix the AC forbids: keyed on the literal property NAME rather than on the template's slots. D1/D2 stay GREEN (differentia really is the missing key there), so only D3 — whose vault spec names `concept__Concept_scope` instead — can tell the two designs apart. That asymmetry is the whole point of D3.
M2_guard_keyed_on_differentia_name._note_anchor: Anchor re-pointed after review LOW-2 replaced the nullable-object `stats` with three primitives; the guard's SEMANTICS are unchanged, only its expression (§A71 — my own edit invalidated the anchor, not drift in someone else's code).
